chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram who dies. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is washed and shrouded in all his garments; he is treated just as the one not in Ihram is treated, except that perfume is not applied to him.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.بِالْمُحِلِّ: The one not in Ihram (free from restrictions)

ai.seo_question: What are the burial rulings for a Muslim who dies while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of Samaanah, a prominent companion of Imam al-Rida, this hadith clarifies that the state of Ihram does not alter the fundamental rites of Ghusl and Kafan, preserving the deceased's dignity by retaining their garments. The specific prohibition of applying perfume (Tayyib) serves as a symbolic continuation of the Ihram state, distinguishing the burial of the pilgrim from that of the ordinary believer while maintaining ritual purity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam, dying’. Heasws said: ‘He would be washed and can be enshrouded with the clothes, all of them. He would be dealt with just as the one not in Ihraam is dealt with, apart from that he would not be touched with the perfume’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who dies in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘Ghusl (bath) and shroud of all pieces must be provided for him like one not in the state of Ihram, except that perfumes must not be allowed to touch him.’”
